SHAEF.wiki: The overall headquarters of the Commander of Allied forces in northwest Europe, from late 1943 until the end of World War II, led by General Dwight D. Eisenhower.

COSSAC.definition: Chief of Staff to the Supreme Allied Commander
COSSAC.wiki: The Allied planning body created in 1943, directed by British Lieutenant-General Frederick E. Morgan, that laid down the foundational operational plans for Operation Overlord.

Mulberry.wiki: Temporary portable artificial harbours developed by the British military to rapidly offload cargo, tanks, and personnel onto Normandy beaches without needing intact captured French ports.

PLUTO.wiki: A major British engineering operation to lay undersea oil pipelines across the English Channel from the Isle of Wight and Dungeness to France, supplying fuel to Allied armies.

LST.wiki: Naval assault ships designed to transport and beach tanks, heavy vehicles, and cargo directly onto hostile shores without requiring dockside cranes or facilities.

LCVP.wiki: Plywood-constructed amphibious landing craft designed by Andrew Higgins, capable of carrying a 36-man platoon or small vehicles from transport ships onto shallow beaches.

C-47.wiki: The military transport aircraft that served as the primary workhorse for Allied airborne operations, dropping paratroopers of the US 82nd and 101st and British 6th Airborne Divisions into Normandy.

OKW.definition: Oberkommando der Wehrmacht (High Command of the German Armed Forces)
OKW.wiki: The supreme military command of Nazi Germany that held direct operational control over the Western Front, reporting directly to Adolf Hitler.

RAF.wiki: The British air warfare branch whose fighter and bomber squadrons maintained overwhelming air superiority over Normandy, flying thousands of sorties to interdict German reinforcements.

USAAF.wiki: The aerial warfare service of the United States Army during World War II, providing heavy tactical and strategic air support across the invasion beachheads.

D-Day.wiki: The designated day on which Operation Overlord was launched, initiating the liberation of German-occupied Western Europe.

H-Hour.wiki: The exact time at which initial assault landing craft hit the beach in a given sector, timed specifically around low tide to avoid submerged German anti-invasion obstacles.
